title: Integrative taxonomy reveals four new species in the superdiverse genus Macrobiotus
summary: GBIF registered a digitized taxonomic treatment of four newly described Macrobiotus species from Asia and Africa, combining morphology, morphometrics, microscopy and four genetic markers. The dataset preserves a machine-readable taxonomic treatment and points back to the 2026 European Journal of Taxonomy article.
semantic_integrity: Taxonomic names and synonymy should be treated as versioned nomenclatural objects; species novelty is supported by the cited integrative evidence, not by the GBIF registration itself.

title: Observation.org, Nature data from around the World
summary: A September 2026 metadata publication covering more than 135,000 species across multiple kingdoms and observations from 1900-present, with more than 175,000 volunteer contributors. A Darwin Core Archive endpoint is provided for machine reuse.
semantic_integrity: Citizen-science observations are evidence records with variable observation uncertainty; contributor volume does not by itself establish taxonomic correctness or sampling representativeness.

title: BioWide Tardigrades
summary: Natural History Museum of Denmark dataset covering eutardigrades from soil samples in the BioWide program, registered in GBIF in September 2026. It provides a focused, reusable biodiversity layer tied to a broader standardized metabarcoding/occurrence workflow.
semantic_integrity: Keep specimen/occurrence identity separate from higher-level ecological interpretation; metabarcoding-derived records require explicit handling of taxonomic resolution.

title: Mid Atlantic marine mammal visual survey in Dec 2025 - Mar 2026
summary: NOAA Northeast Fisheries Science Center survey data published through OBIS-SEAMAP for seasonal North Atlantic right whale distribution, with 198 submitted and accepted occurrences covering six species. The archive is CC0 and retains the original provider attribution.
semantic_integrity: The dataset's explicit quality flags include missing depth fields; these are metadata-quality facts, not evidence that the occurrence observations are invalid.

title: NEON ticks sampled using drag cloths and tick pathogen status
summary: US National Ecological Observatory Network tick surveys using standardized plots and repeated sampling, linked to specimen identification and pathogen testing for Borrelia, Anaplasma, Babesia, Ehrlichia and Rickettsia. The linked-record structure makes it valuable for ecological and disease-vector analyses.
semantic_integrity: Pathogen-positive status is a laboratory observation attached to specimens; it should not be interpreted as human disease incidence without additional epidemiological evidence.

title: Total mercury and methylmercury concentrations in biota collected from the Columbia River Basin, USA
summary: USGS data release published September 18, 2026 containing CSV measurements of total mercury and methylmercury concentrations in biota from the Columbia River Basin.
semantic_integrity: Concentration measurements should remain distinct from causal ecological or human-health claims unless those claims are independently supported.

title: Field maps and notes from geologic mapping by C.M. Wentworth of the Gualala structural block between Fort Ross and Galloway Creek, coastal northern California, 1960-63
summary: Digitized field maps and notes from 1960-63 provide primary observations of structure, faults, bedding attitudes and lithologies in the Gualala block west of the San Andreas fault. This is a strong Fort Knowledge candidate because historical field observations can be reinterpreted without replacing the original observation layer.
semantic_integrity: Historical field terminology and cartographic categories must be preserved alongside any modern reinterpretation; modern geology should be stored as a derivative layer.

title: Age and otolith increments associated with the lower Tallapoosa River catchment
summary: USGS dataset containing fish ages and otolith increment measurements designed to relate age and growth to flow and thermal conditions in the lower Tallapoosa River catchment.
semantic_integrity: Otolith increments are specimen measurements; inferred growth-environment relationships require analysis and uncertainty accounting rather than being assumed from the dataset title.
